chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Uqbah, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, I have grown old and weakened in fasting, so what should I do regarding these three days in every month?' He said, 'O Uqbah, give charity with one dirham for each day.' I said, 'One dirham?' He said, 'Perhaps they are many with you, and you consider the dirham small.' I said, 'Yes, indeed the favors of Allah upon me are abundant.' He said, 'O Uqbah, feeding a Muslim is better than fasting a month.'
ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for someone who cannot fast the three days of the white nights due to old age or weakness?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the fidya (expiation) for those unable to fast due to chronic weakness, prescribing a dirham per day. The Imam’s follow-up question highlights the Shia emphasis on intention and the subjective valuation of wealth, while the concluding statement underscores the superior merit of feeding the needy over prolonged voluntary fasting.
